- Foreign students who earn an associate degree or higher in Taiwan can apply to extend their stay for up to two years. [1]
- During this extended stay, graduates can work without obtaining a separate work permit, and family members can also apply to remain in Taiwan. [1]
- The changes simplify the hiring process by eliminating the need for employers to separately apply to the Ministry of Labor for work permits during the extended stay. [1]
- Graduates are not subject to restrictions on the types of professional or technical jobs they can take, employer qualifications or minimum salary thresholds during the extended stay. [1]

- The 1990 hotline for foreigners in Taiwan is 1990 [3]
- It provides consultation services for foreigners and new residents on matters such as visa, residence, work, education, culture, tax, health insurance, transportation, employment, medical health, personal safety, child upbringing, welfare, legal information, and other life information [3]
- The hotline is available 24 hours a year and is free of charge [3]
- Services are offered in Chinese, English, Japanese, Vietnamese, Indonesian, Thai, and Khmer [3]

- Call 165 for anti-fraud consultation. [1]
- Remember the 3C principle: Calm Down, Check it out, Call 165. [1]

- The employer must pay 10 times the employment insurance premium for each month the student worker is not insured. [1]

- A bachelor's degree takes four years and at least 128 credits in total. [1]
- The university adopts the system of academic years and course credits. [1]
- The Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs (教務處課務組) provides the curriculum table at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw. [1]

- 12 extra graduation credits are required on top of the usual requirements for students admitted on an equivalent qualification from a foreign, Hong Kong, or Macau school that ends at the level of Taiwan's second year of senior high school. Military training and PE do not count toward these 12 credits. [1]
- This requirement is specified in National Central University Study Regulations, Article 48. [1]
- For details, contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs (教務處課務組) at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw. [1]

- At least 16 credits each semester in years one to three and at least 9 in year four. [1]
- National Central University Study Regulations, Article 11: Undergraduate students shall take at least 16 course credits each semester in the first, second, and third academic years and at least 9 course credits each semester in the fourth academic year. [1]

- International students must take the full‑year five‑credit course “Chinese for Overseas Chinese Students” (僑生國文) instead of the regular Chinese (B) course. [1]
- This course counts as the required 5 credits for the Chinese requirement. [1]
- Students who complete “Chinese for Overseas Chinese Students” are not required to take the Chinese (B): Chinese Writing course. [1]
- For details, contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs (教務處課務組) at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw. [1]

- 6 credits of Mandarin courses at the Language Center instead of freshman Chinese [1]
- File for the Chinese course substitution before you graduate [1]
- Contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs (教務處課務組) at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw [1]

- Students must complete five semesters of physical education (PE) (Freshman PE I, Freshman PE II, and three PE interest electives) [1]
- The PE courses do not count toward graduation credits [1]
- After completing the five semesters, students may take an additional 1-credit PE course, which also does not count toward graduation [1]

- A master's degree requires at least 24 credits, not counting thesis credits. [1]
- You must also take at least one graduate course of 1 credit or more at NCU (waived courses do not count). [1]

- At least 34 credits, of which at least 18 are doctoral-level, not counting dissertation credits. [1]
- Contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs (教務處課務組) at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw. [1]

- Apply before the add/drop deadline of your first semester. [1]
- If approved, you skip both semesters and receive 6 credits that count toward graduation. [1]
- Contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs (教務處課務組) at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw. [1]

- Undergraduates must complete at least 100 service hours on the NCU passport before receiving the degree certificate. [1]
- Check your hours on the Service Learning Website (服務學習網) or in the Graduation System (畢業審核系統). [1]
- If you have questions, contact the Center for Service Learning, Office of Student Affairs (學務處服務學習發展中心). [1]
- The announcement is from the Ministry of Education (教務處公告) and dated 115 年 2 月 12 日 (February 12, 2026). [1]

- Service learning is not listed as a graduation condition for master's and doctoral students. [1]
- The graduation conditions include completing all required courses and credits, passing the degree examination, and receiving satisfactory conduct grades each semester. [1]

- For more information, contact the Center for Service Learning, Office of Student Affairs (https://service-learning.ncu.edu.tw/). [1]
